title: I parsed and cleaned 10,809 congressional filings into a single open database of 183,675 trades.
author: NextgenAITrading
selftext:
I parsed and cleaned 10,809 congressional filings into a single open database of 183,675 trades.

Then I open-sourced the pipeline AND the data.

I’ve been open-sourcing trading tools since NexusTrade launched in 2022, but this dataset was harder to build than expected.

Some members of Congress still file their stock trades on paper. The form is filled out by hand, stamped, and scanned in, sometimes sideways. The electronic House filings are PDFs that block you from copying the text. And the same trade can show up again in a later amendment, so a naive count doubles it.

So the pipeline OCRs every scan, reads each filing independently more than once, and reconciles any disagreement against the original page. Every row links back to the official filing.

What's 100% free:

* The raw dataset on Hugging Face (no account or API key needed)
* A one-liner to spin up an SQLite DB locally:
* `npx congressional-disclosures@latest download --sqlite`
* The full parser pipeline on GitHub and npm to build it yourself

It updates daily.

Quiver charges $30/month for this API data. Unusual Whales bundles it into a $50/month tier. This is public data. It should be free.

If you'd rather skip the SQL, the same data powers the Congress research page on NexusTrade. You can research politicians, turn their trades into portfolios, and backtest them.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: amendment reconciliation gets skipped constantly and it quietly ruins the counts. reading each filing more than once and reconciling the disagreement is more than most published versions of this dataset bother with. residual error will sit in the handwritten scans and I cannot see a clean way around that. did you eyeball those or just flag them lower confidence?

replies.author: NextgenAITrading
replies.body: I eyeballed a few! Only one couldn't be extracted using the pipeline, and I've updated the pipeline to describe that edge case.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: One miss out of the ones you eyeballed is better than I'd have guessed for scans. Writing the edge case into the pipeline beats a confidence flag nobody reads.

comments.author: polyglot-a-cracker
comments.body: Have you done any analysis of the data? My instinct is that there will very likely be high correlation between the trades and the stocks’ trending upward (in general) in the relatively short term. But without testing it live there is no way to verify the hypothesis. That’s what I am asking about.

replies.author: NextgenAITrading
replies.body: Yes I did! I plan to publish another article of my results soon. It'll be posted [here](https://nexustrade.io/blog).

replies.author: polyglot-a-cracker
replies.body: Cool, thanks for the link, will check back periodically.
